denomProfiles/jehovahs-witnesses/tagline: Bible-centred movement known for door-to-door preaching and the Watch Tower Society's publications.
denomProfiles/jehovahs-witnesses/coreDoc: Jehovah is the one true God; Jesus is his first creation and Son, not God the Son, and the holy spirit is God's active force.
God's Kingdom, ruling invisibly from heaven since 1914, will soon replace human governments at Armageddon.
Only 144,000 'anointed' go to heaven; other faithful people hope to live forever on a paradise earth.
The soul is mortal; there is no hell of eternal torment.
Political neutrality and refusal of blood transfusions as matters of conscience and obedience.
Mainstream churches reject its Christology and its claims for the Governing Body.
denomProfiles/jehovahs-witnesses/focuses: Public preaching from house to house and with literature carts.
Bible study through Watchtower and other publications.
Separation from politics, war and interfaith activity.
denomProfiles/jehovahs-witnesses/practic: Meetings at Kingdom Halls twice weekly.
Baptism by immersion of committed adult publishers.
Annual Memorial of Christ's death, with emblems taken only by the anointed.
No celebration of Christmas, Easter or birthdays.
The New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures.
denomProfiles/jehovahs-witnesses/influen: Witness lawsuits shaped freedom-of-religion law in the United States, Canada and Europe.
Groups that rejected Rutherford's changes continued as independent Bible Students.
denomProfiles/jehovahs-witnesses/keyFigu: Founder of the Bible Student movement
Second president of the Watch Tower Society (1917–1942)
Third president; expanded training and translation
denomProfiles/jehovahs-witnesses/members: Peak of just over 9 million active publishers in the 2024 service year, with about 21 million attending the Memorial (Jehovah's Witnesses' own report).
denomProfiles/jehovahs-witnesses/inIndia: Congregations meet throughout India, with literature in many Indian languages including Tamil and Malayalam; Witnesses were party to the Supreme Court's Bijoe Emmanuel judgment (1986) on the national anthem.
denomProfiles/unitarian/tagline: Liberal tradition rejecting the Trinity, valuing reason, conscience and freedom of belief.
denomProfiles/unitarian/coreDoctrines/0: God is one person; Jesus is a uniquely inspired human teacher rather than God incarnate.
denomProfiles/unitarian/coreDoctrines/1: Reason and conscience are guides to religious truth alongside Scripture.
denomProfiles/unitarian/coreDoctrines/2: Human goodness and moral improvement rather than original sin.
denomProfiles/unitarian/coreDoctrines/3: Religious freedom and tolerance, as proclaimed in the Edict of Torda (1568).
denomProfiles/unitarian/coreDoctrines/4: In modern Unitarian Universalism, a creedless faith open to many sources beyond Christianity.
denomProfiles/unitarian/focuses/1: Social reform: abolition, women's rights, education and civil rights.
denomProfiles/unitarian/focuses/2: Rational and historical study of the Bible.
denomProfiles/unitarian/practices/0: Congregational worship with readings, hymns and sermon, often without creeds.
denomProfiles/unitarian/practices/1: Infant baptism in Transylvanian and some British churches; child dedications in many UU congregations.
denomProfiles/unitarian/practices/2: Flower Communion, introduced by Norbert Čapek in Prague in 1923.
denomProfiles/unitarian/practices/3: Ordination of women ministers since the nineteenth century.
denomProfiles/unitarian/influenced/0/tex: Rammohun Roy corresponded with Unitarians, and Brahmo theism was shaped by these links.
denomProfiles/unitarian/influenced/1/tex: Emerson and Parker emerged from Unitarian circles.
denomProfiles/unitarian/influenced/2/tex: Unitarian biblical criticism fed wider liberal theology.
denomProfiles/unitarian/keyFigures/1/rol: Founder of the Transylvanian Unitarian Church
denomProfiles/unitarian/inIndia: The Khasi Unitarian Union in Meghalaya traces its origins to Hajom Kissor Singh in 1887, and Unitarian ideas influenced the Brahmo Samaj.
denomProfiles/pentecostal-assemblies-of-: Oldest continuing Oneness Pentecostal body, historically interracial and led by bishops.
One God revealed in Jesus Christ, without distinct persons.
Repentance, baptism in Jesus' name and Spirit baptism with tongues as the new birth.
Holiness of life.
Divine healing.
Evangelism and church planting, especially among African Americans.
Episcopal oversight by a council of bishops.
Holiness and family life.
Overseas missions in Africa, the Caribbean and Asia.
Baptism by immersion in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.
Exuberant worship with gospel music and tongues.
Communion and foot washing.
Women serve as ministers and missionaries, though the episcopate has been male.
United Pentecostal Church International
White members who left the PAW in 1924 eventually formed bodies that merged into the UPCI.
Gospel music
Haywood's hymns, such as 'Jesus, the Son of God', entered Pentecostal hymnody.
Garfield T. Haywood
First Presiding Bishop (1925–1931)
J. J. Frazee
Early general chairman
denomProfiles/united-pentecostal-church-: Largest Oneness Pentecostal denomination, known for Acts 2:38 preaching and holiness standards.
One God, fully revealed in Jesus Christ; the Trinity of persons is rejected.
The new birth is repentance, baptism in Jesus' name and receiving the Holy Spirit with tongues.
Holiness of life, including outward standards of dress.
Divine healing and the premillennial return of Christ.
Global missions and church planting.
Bible colleges and ministerial training.
Holiness 'standards' and separation from worldliness.
Revival and evangelism.
Baptism by immersion in the name of Jesus.
Spirit-filled worship with tongues, music and altar prayer.
Women generally wear long hair and dresses; television and adornment discouraged historically.
Women may hold a ministerial licence, though senior offices are held by men.
Oneness churches worldwide
Its missionaries founded national United Pentecostal churches in many countries.
Howard A. Goss
First general superintendent
David K. Bernard
General superintendent and theologian of Oneness doctrine
UPCI missionaries work in India, and the separately organised United Pentecostal Church (North East India) is a major denomination in Mizoram.
denomProfiles/iglesia-ni-cristo/tagline: Filipino church holding Felix Manalo as God's last messenger restoring the true church.
denomProfiles/iglesia-ni-cristo/coreDoct: God the Father is the only true God; Jesus is a man, Son of God and Saviour, but not God.
The original church apostatised; the true Church of Christ re-emerged in the Philippines on 27 July 1914.
Felix Manalo is the 'angel from the east' of Revelation 7 and God's last messenger.
Membership in the Iglesia ni Cristo is necessary for salvation.
Mainstream churches reject its Christology and its claim to be the only true church.
denomProfiles/iglesia-ni-cristo/focuses/: Unity and discipline under the Executive Minister.
Evangelism and rapid expansion, including abroad.
Large chapel-building programme with distinctive architecture.
Bloc voting in Philippine elections as an expression of unity.
denomProfiles/iglesia-ni-cristo/practice: Twice-weekly worship services with set doctrinal lessons.
denomProfiles/iglesia-ni-cristo/influenc: Became one of the largest and most influential religious bodies in the Philippines.
denomProfiles/iglesia-ni-cristo/members/: About 2.8 million (roughly 2.6 per cent of the population) in the Philippine Statistics Authority's 2020 census; the church gives no official count.
denomProfiles/true-jesus-church/tagline: Chinese indigenous Pentecostal church keeping the Sabbath and baptising in Jesus' name.
denomProfiles/true-jesus-church/coreDoct: One God, revealed in Jesus Christ; Oneness rather than trinitarian theology.
Five doctrines (with Sabbath and foot washing): Spirit baptism with tongues, water baptism, foot washing, Holy Communion and the Sabbath.
Water baptism by full immersion, face downward, in living water, in the name of Jesus.
The True Jesus Church as the restored church of the latter rain.
Mainstream churches question its exclusive claims and Oneness teaching.
denomProfiles/true-jesus-church/practice: Prayer together aloud in tongues, kneeling.
Holy Communion with one loaf of unleavened bread and grape juice.
Separation of men and women in seating in many congregations.
denomProfiles/true-jesus-church/influenc: A strand of indigenous Pentecostal piety in Chinese Christianity.
denomProfiles/christadelphians/tagline: Lay-led Bible community awaiting Christ's return to establish God's Kingdom on earth.
denomProfiles/christadelphians/coreDoctr: God is one; Jesus is the Son of God, born of Mary, not pre-existent; the Holy Spirit is God's power.
Humans are mortal; the hope is bodily resurrection, not an immortal soul.
The Kingdom of God will be established on earth, centred on Israel, at Christ's return.
The devil is understood as human sin, not a personal fallen angel.
Belief of the gospel and baptism by immersion are necessary for salvation.
denomProfiles/christadelphians/focuses/0: Bible reading and study, aided by Robert Roberts's daily 'Bible Companion'.
denomProfiles/christadelphians/focuses/1: Expectation of Christ's return and attention to prophecy and Israel.
denomProfiles/christadelphians/practices: No paid clergy; brothers take turns to preside and exhort.
Baptism of believers by immersion after examination.
denomProfiles/christadelphians/influence: An influential voice for mortalism within dissenting Protestantism.
denomProfiles/christadelphians/keyFigure: Organiser and editor of The Christadelphian
denomProfiles/christian-science/tagline: Church founded by Mary Baker Eddy teaching healing through spiritual understanding of God.
denomProfiles/christian-science/coreDoct: God is infinite Mind, Spirit, Life, Truth and Love; matter, sin and disease are not ultimately real.
Jesus is the Way-shower who demonstrated the Christ, divine truth, but is not himself God.
Healing comes through prayer that corrects mistaken material belief.
The Bible and Eddy's 'Science and Health with Key to the Scriptures' are the church's pastor.
Mainstream churches reject its denial of the reality of matter and its non-trinitarian theology.
denomProfiles/christian-science/focuses/: Spiritual healing in place of medical treatment.
Reading rooms and publishing, including The Christian Science Monitor.
Daily study of the Bible Lesson.
Practitioners who give healing treatment through prayer.
denomProfiles/christian-science/practice: Sunday services with readings from the Bible and Science and Health by lay Readers.
No sacraments with physical elements; baptism and communion are understood spiritually.
Governance by the Church Manual and the Mother Church in Boston.
denomProfiles/christian-science/influenc: The New Thought movement, including Unity, drew on Christian Science ideas.
Former Christian Scientists such as Emma Curtis Hopkins spread mental-healing teaching.
denomProfiles/unity-church/tagline: New Thought movement teaching practical Christianity, positive prayer and the divinity in every person.
denomProfiles/unity-church/coreDoctrines: God is divine Mind, present everywhere and in everyone.
Jesus is the great example of humanity realising the Christ within.
Thoughts and words shape experience; affirmative prayer brings health and prosperity.
Openness to truth in all religions and to reincarnation, which the founders accepted.
denomProfiles/unity-church/focuses/1: Prayer ministry through Silent Unity, active since 1890.
denomProfiles/unity-church/practices/0: Sunday services with music, meditation and a talk.
denomProfiles/unity-church/practices/2: Ordination of women and men as ministers.
denomProfiles/unity-church/practices/3: Burning bowl and other symbolic rituals rather than sacraments.
denomProfiles/unity-church/influenced/0/: Unity's literature spread affirmative prayer widely.
